# /crav1-map-pipeline-environments

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [From Azure DevOps pipelines](../../from-pipeline-environments.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-map-pipeline-environments/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Read Azure DevOps pipeline definitions for the org and project the user named.

When the user names Azure DevOps, the org, and the project, **[`/crav1-map-pipeline-environments`](crav1-map-pipeline-environments.md)** reads those pipeline definitions and proposes environment marks. A pipeline name is optional. It lists and shows with `az pipelines` and `az devops`. It does not run a pipeline. The stage name gives the environment, with the same whole-word rule as [`/crav1-read-environment`](crav1-read-environment.md). A deploy step marks the resource it names. The group is context. It appends only confirmed lines to `docs/environments/marks.md`. It does not write the system, architecture, feature, or left-out files. It is cross-cutting. It is a later skill. It is not a starter option. Asking for startup options names only the six and does not run this command. It names [`/crav1-read-environment`](crav1-read-environment.md) and does not run it.

## Runs when

The user names Azure DevOps, the org, and the project. Called by the user.

## Reads

In short: Those pipeline definitions and `marks.md`.

Reads Azure DevOps pipeline definitions for the org and project the user named, and `docs/environments/marks.md` when it exists.

## Writes

In short: Confirmed lines on `docs/environments/marks.md`.

Writes only confirmed lines appended to `docs/environments/marks.md`.

## Does not

Leaves `docs/system`, `docs/architecture/spec.md`, feature specs, `docs/architecture/left-out.md`, and application code alone.

Limits and exceptions: Azure DevOps, the org, or the project missing stops the read. A missing CLI, extension, or login stops it. It does not run a pipeline. It names [`/crav1-read-environment`](crav1-read-environment.md) and does not run it. It is not a starter option.
